candidate.O9_family: CWE-863 incorrect authorization: principal mis-derivation (shared admin account) plus open-by-default fallback applied to authenticated callers
candidate.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Tighten only ListTableBuckets' per-bucket filter (or its account gate) in the S3 Tables handler, leaving getAccountID's admin-account mapping and the Iceberg Manager default-allow untouched.

verified.exploit_entry_point: Signed (SigV4) S3 Tables API requests (POST / with X-Amz-Target) to the S3 gateway's real S3 Tables routes (registerS3TablesRoutes + authenticateS3Tables) with identities loaded by the real config loader from an s3.json document; Iceberg REST catalog requests to iceberg.NewServer(s3a, s3a) as weed/command/s3.go wires it, and to the same server with an embedding's own authenticator; weed shell s3tables.bucket commands. All backed by an in-memory filer served over loopback gRPC.

wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the only adjusting step on caller values is principal normalisation (ARN suffix, trim); every tested principal is already in normal form and the admin-name guard compares the normalised value, so no guard can sit before an adjustment that changes a tested input
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: identities come from the real config loader, SigV4 verification and the authenticator interface; no tested route parses a caller-supplied identity spelling, so there is no parser pair that could disagree

traps.shape: principal mis-derivation: identity in the shared admin account without admin permissions (explicit member, or an identity whose configured account does not exist, which the config loader maps to the admin account)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the admin account is a configured account; membership looks like intent, and the producer is the S3 config loader in another file

traps.shape: open-by-default fallback applied to authenticated callers on every handler (28 policy contexts in 5 files) of a gateway with static identities
traps.reason_to_dismiss: default-allow is the documented zero-config behaviour; fixing the listing (the report's trigger) looks sufficient

traps.shape: defaults route in a second front end: the Iceberg catalog's manager is forced open regardless of its authenticator, and a caller reported by name only is treated as unauthenticated
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the manager is documented as a helper for shell/admin tooling, and the catalog is a separate REST protocol in another package

traps.shape: client-asserted principal: a request without credentials carries the server's internal account header (value = admin, or = the owner's account) and is treated as that principal, bypassing an explicit Deny
traps.reason_to_dismiss: only reachable when the gateway is open to requests without credentials anyway

traps.shape: identity-provider attribute equal to the admin name (preferred_username/sub) becomes the admin principal without admin permissions
traps.reason_to_dismiss: claims come from the trusted identity provider; the advisory is about static identities sharing the admin account

traps.shape: a caller known to an embedding authenticator only by the name 'admin' (no identity object, no admin permissions) becomes the admin principal through the catalog's manager; only trusted local tools (shell, admin console, weed mini) may act as admin by name
traps.where: weed/s3api/s3tables/handler.go:223-233 (name-only and header fallbacks), weed/s3api/s3tables/permissions.go:100-103; entry weed/s3api/s3tables/manager.go Execute via weed/s3api/iceberg
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the admin console relies on acting as 'admin' by name through the same manager
